text: The rwb-source-data payment product, the rwb-case state read and move answer, the rwb-partner scorecard and the rwb-access right are consumed on their owners' published contracts, never as tables or views, and their operation names stay placeholders until the owners publish them.
why: Only rwb-source-data reads the 30 recovery.v_ace_* views, only rwb-case writes recovery_case, only rwb-partner holds the buyer scorecard and only rwb-access answers a right, while TSD S6 T5.2 names the published interfaces only as module interfaces and publishes no operation name for these reads, so no name may be invented. The plan's C row for the slice is empty, so the rows are C dependencies in fact and not in the metadata.

impact: The app story builds on Day 1 against six contract fakes and the event fake with a 2 s budget and a breaker, and a statement on a v_ace_* view or a recovery_case row fails the boundary test

text: The Debt sale rule package is read as data at its version in force and evaluated by this service's own evaluator inside the workflow activity; no embedded Drools kit row is added to the metadata, so RWB-PLT-E1072-CON and RWB-P7-E1073-CON are recorded as absent.
why: DP-04 is not in the pattern set the plan gives this key, yet the step evaluates the DEBTSALE route set of 41 rules over 29 states and the architecture places rule evaluation inside the owning service's activity. Keeping the plan's H row unchanged and recording the kit as a tracked dependency is the only choice that does not invent a metadata value.

text: The settlement outcome is held in the decision record, the case move answer and the release of the transfer step, because no column of debt_sale_lot or debt_sale_account carries a settlement date, a matched amount or a proceeds reference; the stamp is recorded for the DB story and not added by this build.
why: TSD S6 T3.1 declares eleven lot fields and seven account fields and none of them is a settlement fact, and LOV-LOT-STATUS has no SETTLED member, so writing a settlement date or a settled status here would invent a column and a list value. The decision record is the only contracted carrier of the outcome that exists in the baseline.
read: TSD S6 T3.1 and T3.2; FSD S6 A2.15.2; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 rows R-DS-25 to R-DS-27; Template and Rules v1 R9
applied_in: RWB-S6-E6011-APP sections 2, 3, 4, 9, 11 and 13; RWB-S6-E6011-CON sections 7 AC2 and AC7, 11, 12.7 and 19
confirm: Solution architect and the data steward of the S6 DB story, before the DB story is tagged
impact: The build writes no business column of the lot and proves the outcome on the decision record and the case move; the DB story adds the stamp in a later additive migration

text: The trigger of the settle-and-cancel step is the rwb.payment.ProceedsMatched.v1 event of rwb-payment (event 25), consumed with one consumer group, an inbox row keyed by the event ID and the owner's dead-letter topic, although FSD S6 A2.15.4.4 declares no background event for the feature.
why: The architecture gives rwb-debtsale an IN subscription to ProceedsMatched with the payload proceedsId, caseId and amount, the connection matrix puts an event edge from S6 to P8, and the FSD's 'No background event' row contradicts its own step 1, which names an event as one of three triggers. Source precedence puts the architecture above the FSD, so the event stands and the conflict is recorded rather than smoothed.

impact: The step is event-started and writes one inbox row per event; a duplicate event is answered from the inbox and produces no second effect, and the envelope fields stay placeholders until the owner publishes them

text: The buyer score of R-DS-26 is a scorecard fact of rwb-partner (S9) and is referenced in the decision record as a score reference with its band; no score is computed in rwb-debtsale and the account score product v_ace_score is not the buyer score.
why: Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 says R-DS-26 scores the cancellation against the buyer, Architecture v5 slide 41 gives rwb-partner the scorecards, and the legacy Data table's v_ace_score carries account_key and score_value of an account, not of a buyer. Inventing a score formula, a threshold or a score column in rwb_debtsale would be a business value.

impact: The cancellation records a score reference and a band, the score itself stays with rwb-partner, and the build carries no score threshold

text: The ACE payment and score facts of the awarded accounts are read only through the rwb-source-data contract, and the branch of DP-05 that allows a service's own ACE views is treated as closed by Architecture v5 slide 8.
why: The pattern offers two branches and the target closes one: the 30 recovery.v_ace_* views are read only by rwb-source-data, so a SELECT on recovery.v_ace_payment from rwb_debtsale would break the boundary the architecture draws. Recording the closure keeps the pattern's intent, one hop to the owner, and prevents a build from taking the second branch.

text: The legacy feature dependency FEAT-DBS-12, derecognize and post to the general ledger, is a sibling story of rwb-debtsale that the plan's H row for this key does not carry, so it is tracked as a build input of the settlement and not added to the metadata.
why: The legacy story names FEAT-DBS-12 as its prerequisite and the FSD keeps it as the prerequisite of A2.15, while the plan's H row gives only the CON story and the two platform CON stories. Adding a story identifier that the plan does not allocate would invent a key; dropping the dependency would let the settlement be built before the derecognition exists.
